facts.statement: The holotype specimen PVL 3827 was found in the Los Colorados Formation in northwestern Argentina.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, PVL 3827, was found in the Los Colorados Formation of the Ischigualasto-Villa Unión Basin in northwestern Argentina.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen PVL 3827 consists of a complete skull, mandibles, and a nearly complete postcranial skeleton collected in the late 1960s.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen is PVL 3827, consisting of a complete skull and mandibles, as well as a nearly complete postcranial skeleton, and it was collected during the late 1960s.

facts.statement: Three other specimens are known, including PVL 3828 which is almost as complete as the holotype and includes a nearly complete skull.
facts.quote: Three other specimens are known. PVL 3828 is almost as complete as the holotype, including a nearly complete skull.

facts.statement: Its family, Ornithosuchidae, consisted of facultatively bipedal pseudosuchians with adaptations for scavenging.
facts.quote: Ornithosuchidae was a widespread family of facultatively bipedal pseudosuchians (crocodilian-line archosaurs) with adaptations for scavenging.

facts.statement: A 2026 study of the snout's neurovascular anatomy suggests a sensory system similar to extant crocodilians and birds, supporting wading-foraging behavior.
facts.quote: Ulloa-Guaiquin et al. (2026) study the neurovascular anatomy of the snout of Riojasuchus tenuisceps, interpreted as consistent with presence of sensory system similar to those seen in extant crocodilians and birds, and supporting a wading-foraging behavior of the studied ornithosuchid.

facts.statement: The time range is recorded as Norian to Norian (227.3 to 205.7 million years ago).
facts.quote: Time range: Norian to Norian (227.3 to 205.7 million years ago)
